summary: Source-based expansion of the arithmetic side of derived Ihara avoidance and ultrapatching in Allen–Calegari–Caraiani–Gee–Helm–Le Hung–Newton–Scholze–Taylor–Thorne, "Potential automorphy over CM fields" (published Annals 197 (2023) version; its section numbering §§2–7 agrees with the README matrix). PA.3: the pair of global deformation problems S_1, S_χ congruent modulo ϖ with twisted coefficients V_λ(χ⁻¹) (§6.5.1, §6.6.1); the dimension/component hypotheses of Assumption 6.3.6 from Lemmas 6.2.26–6.2.27; Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations of type S_χ (Propositions 6.5.3, 6.6.7); the generic support implications of the Fontaine–Laffaille (full support) and ordinary (pointwise) cases; and a comparison with Calegari–Geraghty Theorem 9.19 recording that ACC+ circumvents, rather than proves, the integral degree-vanishing part of CG Conjecture B. PA.4: Taylor–Wiles local conditions and data (§6.2.18, §6.2.28), existence of data killing the dual Selmer group (Lemma 6.2.32) with g = qn − n²[F⁺:Q] patching variables (Proposition 6.2.33), auxiliary level subgroups, Hecke algebras and maximal ideals (Lemma 6.5.8), Taylor–Wiles level-change isomorphisms (Lemma 6.5.9), O[Δ_Q]-linear Galois representations (Proposition 6.5.11), verification that the Fontaine–Laffaille tower satisfies the ultrapatching set-up of §6.4.1 with specialization C_∞/a_∞ ≅ C_0, and the resulting Theorem 6.5.4/Corollary 6.5.5. PA.0: Theorem 2.4.10 (rational cohomology concentration in [q₀, q₀ + l₀]). The abstract §§6.3–6.4 algebra is linked to DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8/P9 rather than duplicated. Recorded misprints: g printed as qn − n[F⁺:Q] on pp. 1070 and 1081; "Proposition 6.2.32" for 6.2.33 on p. 1068; "/(λ)" for "/(ϖ)" in Lemma 6.2.27(1). Unread imports (Khare–Thorne 2017, Taylor 2008, BLGHT 2011, Bellaïche–Chenevier 2009, ACC+ Theorem 3.1.1, Franke–Schwermer) are gaps. PA.1, PA.2 and PA.5 are not yet decomposed in this revision.

nodes.title: Rational cohomology of X_K localized at m with ρ̄_m absolutely irreducible is cuspidal and concentrated in [q₀, q₀ + l₀] (ACC+ Theorem 2.4.10)
nodes.statement: Setting of ACC+ §2.2: F an imaginary CM field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺, p a prime, E/Q_p finite containing all embeddings of F, O its ring of integers, S a finite set of finite places of F containing the p-adic places, K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) a good (neat, product) subgroup with K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for v ∉ S, λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, V_λ the integral dual Weyl module lattice, T^S(K, V_λ) the image of T^S = H(GL_n^S, K^S) ⊗ O in End_{D(O)}(RΓ(X_K, V_λ)). Fix ι: Q̄_p ≅ C. (1) If π is a cuspidal regular algebraic automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) of weight ιλ with (π^∞)^K ≠ 0, the homomorphism T^S → Q̄_p given by the Hecke eigenvalues of (ι⁻¹π^∞)^K factors through T^S(K, λ). (2) Put q₀ = [F⁺:Q]·n(n−1)/2 and l₀ = [F⁺:Q]·n − 1. If m ⊂ T^S(K, V_λ) is a maximal ideal with ρ̄_m absolutely irreducible, then H^j(X_K, V_λ)_m[1/p] ≠ 0 only for j ∈ [q₀, q₀ + l₀], and if one of these groups in the range is nonzero then all are; every homomorphism f: T^S(K, V_λ)_m → Q̄_p is the Hecke eigensystem of (ι⁻¹π^∞)^K for a cuspidal regular algebraic π of weight ιλ, and then the reduction of r_ι(π) is isomorphic to ρ̄_m. The conclusion is only after inverting p: nothing is asserted about torsion in H^j(X_K, V_λ)_m outside [q₀, q₀ + l₀].
hypotheses: m must admit an absolutely irreducible residual Galois representation ρ̄_m (m of Galois type and non-Eisenstein, ACC+ Definition 2.3.6); its existence for maximal ideals in the support of cohomology is ACC+ Theorem 2.3.5 under S = S^c and the imaginary-quadratic splitting condition on residue characteristics.
The degree count uses F imaginary CM: the Lie algebra m_G is a sum of the (gl_n(C), U(n)) pieces at the [F⁺:Q] complex places and an abelian Lie algebra of dimension [F⁺:Q] − 1.

Imported and unread here: Franke [Fra98, Th. 18] (automorphic description of H*(X_K, V)), Franke–Schwermer [FS98, §2.2 and Prop. 3.3] (decomposition along associate classes of parabolics and description of the summands by parabolic induction of cuspidal data), Borel–Wallach [BW00, Ch. II, Prop. 3.1], Clozel [Clo90, Lem. 3.14], and ACC+ Theorem 2.3.2 (the main theorem of HLTT) for Galois representations of regular algebraic cuspidal representations of GL_m, m ≤ n.
proofSteps: Pass to complex coefficients: H^j(X_K, V_ιλ)_m := H^j(X_K, V_λ)_m ⊗_{O,ι} C; part (2) reduces to degree bounds, all-or-nothing nonvanishing in the range, and cuspidality of each Hecke eigensystem in H*(X_K, V_ιλ)_m (ACC+ proof of Thm 2.4.10, p. 949).

Franke’s theorem [Fra98, Th. 18], as in [FS98, §2.2], gives a canonical decomposition H*(X_K, V_ιλ) = (⊕_{{Q}} H*(m_G, K_∞; A_{V_ιλ,{Q}} ⊗ V_ιλ)(χ_λ))^K over associate classes {Q} of parabolic Q-subgroups of Res_{F/Q} GL_n; the summand for {G} is cuspidal cohomology ⊕_π (π^∞)^K ⊗ H*(m_G, K_∞; π_∞ ⊗ V_ιλ).

By [FS98, Prop. 3.3] (see also the proof of [Fra98, Th. 20]) a maximal ideal M of the prime-to-S Hecke algebra ⊗ C in the support of E^K_{Q} is the eigensystem of the unnormalized induction from Q of a cuspidal σ = ⊠π_i on L_Q with π_i regular algebraic (weight determined by some w ∈ W^Q); ACC+ explains how this follows from the filtration argument in the proof of [FS98, Prop. 3.3] (pp. 949–950).

By ACC+ Theorem 2.3.2 there is r_ι(M) = ⊕_i r_ι(π_i) ⊗ ε^{−(n_{i+1}+⋯+n_r)} with the right Frobenius polynomials; for proper Q this is reducible, contradicting absolute irreducibility of ρ̄_m, so (E^K_{Q})_m = 0 for every proper Q (p. 951).

For cuspidal π with the matching central character on R_{>0}: H*(m_G, K_∞; π_∞ ⊗ V_ιλ) = 0 unless π is regular algebraic of weight ιλ [BW00, Ch. II, Prop. 3.1]; if it is, the groups are nonzero exactly in degrees [q₀, q₀ + l₀] by [Clo90, Lem. 3.14] and the Künneth formula, the range being (n − 1)[F⁺:Q] + [F⁺:Q] − 1 = l₀ (p. 951). Part (1) is the corresponding statement that the eigenvector for (π^∞)^K occurs in cohomology.
acceptance: GL₁ sanity check (n = 1): q₀ = 0 and l₀ = [F⁺:Q] − 1, the rank of the unit group of the CM field F, i.e. the degrees of the cohomology of the tori making up X_K.
n = 2, F imaginary quadratic: q₀ = 1 and l₀ = 1, the degrees 1 and 2 in which cuspidal cohomology of Bianchi manifolds occurs.
Record explicitly that the statement is after inverting p; integral vanishing outside [q₀, q₀ + l₀] is Calegari–Geraghty Conjecture B(4)(a), which ACC+ does not prove.

nodes.title: The pair of global deformation problems S_1, S_χ congruent modulo ϖ, and the twisted coefficient modules V_λ(χ⁻¹) (ACC+ §6.5.1, §6.6.1)
nodes.statement: Fontaine–Laffaille set-up (ACC+ §6.5.1). Data: F imaginary CM; n ≥ 2 and a prime p > n²; a finite set S of finite places containing S_p; a possibly empty R ⊂ S of places prime to p; π cuspidal regular algebraic of weight λ; ι: Q̄_p ≅ C; subject to conditions (6)–(17) (listed under hypotheses). Level: K = ∏_v K_v with K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for v ∉ S or v | p, K_v = Iw_v for v ∈ R, K_v = Iw_{v,1} (pro-v Iwahori) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p); K is neat (Lemma 6.5.2), hence good. By Theorem 2.4.10 there are E and a maximal ideal m ⊂ T^S(K, V_λ) with ρ̄_m ≅ r̄_ι(π); enlarge E so that the residue field of m is k. For every tuple χ = (χ_{v,i})_{v∈R, 1≤i≤n} of characters χ_{v,i}: k(v)^× → O^× trivial modulo ϖ, define S_χ = (ρ̄_m, S, {O}_{v∈S}, {D_v^FL}_{v∈S_p} ∪ {D_v^χ}_{v∈R} ∪ {D_v^□}_{v∈S−(R∪S_p)}), where D_v^FL is the Fontaine–Laffaille problem of Proposition 6.2.14, D_v^□ is the unrestricted lifting functor, and D_v^χ (§6.2.15, for q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial, p > n) is the functor of lifts ρ with char_{ρ(σ)}(X) = ∏_{i=1}^{n} (X − χ_i(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))) for all σ ∈ I_{F_v}. Fix representatives ρ_{S_χ} of the universal deformations identified modulo ϖ via R_{S_χ}/ϖ ≅ R_{S_1}/ϖ. Coefficients: V_λ(χ⁻¹) = V_λ ⊗_O O(χ⁻¹), K_S acting on V_λ through K_p and on O(χ⁻¹) through K_S → K_R = ∏_{v∈R} Iw_v → ∏_{v∈R} (k(v)^×)^n; in particular V_λ(1) = V_λ and V_λ(χ⁻¹)/ϖ = V_λ/ϖ. The local problems defining S_χ are formally smooth away from R. In the proof of Theorem 6.5.4, after enlarging E to contain a primitive p-th root of unity, p > n allows each χ_v = (χ_{v,1},…,χ_{v,n}) to be chosen pairwise distinct. Ordinary set-up (ACC+ §6.6.1, p > n): K_v = Iw_v(1,1) at v ∈ S_p; Λ_v = Λ_{1,v}/℘_{0,v} with Λ_{1,v} = O[[O_{F_v}^×(p)^n]] and ℘_{0,v} the unique minimal prime contained in ker(p_{μ,v}); Λ = ⊗̂_{v∈S_p} Λ_v; for characters χ: K_R → O^× trivial modulo ϖ, S_χ = (ρ̄_m, S, {O}_{v∈S−S_p} ∪ {Λ_v}_{v∈S_p}, {D_v^{det,ord}}_{v∈S_p} ∪ {D_v^χ}_{v∈R} ∪ {D_v^□}_{v∈S−(R∪S_p)}) and V_μ(χ⁻¹) = V_μ ⊗_O O(χ⁻¹), with m ⊂ T^S(K, μ)^{ord} of residue field k and ρ̄_m ≅ r̄_ι(π).
hypotheses: FL case (ACC+ §6.5.1): (6) every prime below S or ramified in F splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F (so S is split over F⁺ and F/F⁺ is everywhere unramified); (7) p unramified in F; (8) λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,n} − λ_{τc,n} < p − 2n for every τ: F ↪ C; (9) for each v ∈ S_p with v̄ below it there is v̄′ ≠ v̄ above p with Σ_{v̄″ ≠ v̄, v̄′} [F⁺_{v̄″}:Q_p] > ½[F⁺:Q]; (10) r̄_ι(π) absolutely irreducible; (11) π_v unramified for v | p; (12) π_v^{Iw_v} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R; (13) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p): π_v unramified, v ∉ R^c, H²(F_v, ad r̄_ι(π)) = 0; (14) S − (R ∪ S_p) contains two places of distinct residue characteristics; (15) π_v unramified for v ∉ S; (16) q_v ≡ 1 mod p and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} trivial for v ∈ R; (17) r̄_ι(π) decomposed generic and r̄_ι(π)(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous.

Ordinary case (ACC+ §6.6.1): p > n; (7) r̄_ι(π) absolutely irreducible; (8) π_v^{Iw_v(1,1)} ≠ 0 and π ι-ordinary at v ∈ S_p ([Ger19, Def. 5.3]); (15) [F_v:Q_p] > n(n+1)/2 + 1 and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} trivial for v ∈ S_p; the other conditions as in the FL case (numbering (6), (9)–(14)).
Standing assumptions of ACC+ §6.2: ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and p ∤ 2n; the determinant is not fixed (Definition 6.2.2 differs from [CG18, §8.5.2] and [KT17, Def. 4.2] in this respect).
Imported without proof in the source: that D_v^χ is a local deformation problem (asserted in §6.2.15); Proposition 6.2.14 (D_v^FL), which "follows from [CHT08, §2.4.1] and a twisting argument".
proofSteps: Neatness (Lemma 6.5.2): if (g_v, g_{v′}) ∈ Iw_{v,1} × Iw_{v′,1} with residue characteristics q ≠ q′ and Γ_v ∩ Γ_{v′} contained a root of unity ζ of prime order q″, then ζ − 1 lies in the maximal ideal at v and at v′, forcing q″ = q and q″ = q′ (printed p. 1062).
Existence of m with ρ̄_m ≅ r̄_ι(π): Theorem 2.4.10(1) places the Hecke eigensystem of (ι⁻¹π^∞)^K in T^S(K, λ); its maximal ideal m then has ρ̄_m ≅ r̄_ι(π) (printed p. 1062).

Congruence modulo ϖ: since every χ_{v,i} ≡ 1 mod ϖ, the conditions defining D_v^χ and D_v^1 coincide on coefficient rings killed by ϖ, which is the source of the canonical identifications R_{S_χ}/ϖ ≅ R_{S_1}/ϖ and R^loc/ϖ ≅ R′^loc/ϖ used on printed p. 1068; likewise O(χ⁻¹)/ϖ is the trivial module, so RΓ(X_K, V_λ(χ⁻¹)) ⊗^L_O k ≅ RΓ(X_K, V_λ) ⊗^L_O k compatibly with T^S (the source states these identifications as canonical without further argument; the explanation here is a reviewer reading).
Distinct characters: with ζ_p ∈ E and q_v ≡ 1 mod p, k(v)^× has a quotient of order p, giving p characters trivial modulo ϖ; p > n allows n pairwise distinct ones (printed p. 1068).
acceptance: Check on a toy case (n = 2, one place v ∈ R with q_v ≡ 1 mod p) that D_v^χ and D_v^1 define the same subfunctor on Artinian k-algebras.
Keep S_1 (unipotent inertial characteristic polynomial) and S_χ (pairwise distinct characters) as two distinct problems: only their reductions modulo ϖ are identified.
In the ordinary case the coefficient ring is Λ, not O; record which statements are over Λ.

nodes.title: The patched deformation rings R_∞, R′_∞ satisfy the dimension and component hypotheses (1)–(2) of Assumption 6.3.6 (ACC+ Lemmas 6.2.26–6.2.27 and their use in §§6.5–6.6)
nodes.statement: Let T = S = S_p ⊔ R ⊔ S_a with S_a = S − (R ∪ S_p). (FL, Lemma 6.2.26.) Assume F_v/Q_p unramified and ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} Fontaine–Laffaille as in Proposition 6.2.14 with D_v = D_v^FL for v ∈ S_p; q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial and D_v = D_v^{χ_v} with χ_{v,i}: O_{F_v}^× → O^× trivial modulo ϖ for v ∈ R; H²(F_v, ad ρ̄) = 0 and D_v = D_v^□ for v ∈ S_a. (1) If all χ_{v,i} = 1, Spec R^{T,loc}_S is equidimensional of dimension 1 + n²|T| + (n(n−1)/2)[F:Q], every generic point has characteristic 0, and every generic point of Spec R^{T,loc}_S/ϖ is the specialization of a unique generic point of Spec R^{T,loc}_S. (2) If χ_{v,1},…,χ_{v,n} are pairwise distinct for each v ∈ R, Spec R^{T,loc}_S is irreducible of dimension 1 + n²|T| + (n(n−1)/2)[F:Q] with characteristic-0 generic point. (Ordinary, Lemma 6.2.27.) Replace the conditions at v ∈ S_p by [F_v:Q_p] > n(n+1)/2 + 1, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial, Λ_v = O[[O_{F_v}^×(p)^n]]/℘_v for a minimal prime ℘_v and D_v = D_v^{det,ord}. (1) If all χ_{v,i} = 1: dim Spec R^{T,loc}_S = 1 + n²|T| + (n(n+1)/2)[F:Q]; components of maximum dimension have characteristic-0 generic points; every other component has dimension ≤ n²|T| − 1 + (n(n+1)/2)[F:Q]; every maximum-dimensional component of Spec R^{T,loc}_S/(ϖ) (printed "/(λ)") is the specialization of a unique generic point. (2) If the χ_{v,i} are pairwise distinct: the same dimension, a unique component of maximum dimension, with characteristic-0 generic point, all others of dimension ≤ n²|T| − 1 + (n(n+1)/2)[F:Q]. (3) A point on a component of non-maximum dimension maps, for some v ∈ S_p, into the closed locus χ_i^univ = χ_j^univ (i ≠ j) of Spec Λ_v. Consequence (proof of Theorem 6.5.4): with q = h¹(F_S/F, ad ρ̄_m(1)), g = qn − n²[F⁺:Q], S_∞ = T[[Z_p^{nq}]] where T is a power series ring over O in n²|S| − 1 variables (so dim S_∞ = n²|S| + qn), R_∞ = R^{S,loc}_{S_1}[[X_1,…,X_g]] and R′_∞ = R^{S,loc}_{S_χ}[[X_1,…,X_g]] (χ_v pairwise distinct), one has dim R_∞ = dim R′_∞ = 1 + g + n²|S| + (n(n−1)/2)[F:Q] = dim S_∞ − l₀ with l₀ = n[F⁺:Q] − 1, each generic point of Spec R_∞/ϖ specializes from a unique generic point of Spec R_∞, all generic points of R_∞ have characteristic 0, and Spec R′_∞ is irreducible with characteristic-0 generic point; hence hypotheses (1)–(2) of Assumption 6.3.6. In the ordinary proof of Theorem 6.6.2, Lemma 6.2.27(1)–(2) give hypotheses (1)–(2) of §6.3.5 (with T a power series ring over Λ).
hypotheses: p ∤ 2n and ρ̄ absolutely irreducible (standing in ACC+ §6.2); T = S nonempty.

Local inputs imported by the source and not read here: Proposition 6.2.14 (R_v^FL formally smooth over O of dimension 1 + n² + (n(n−1)/2)[F_v:Q_p]; from [CHT08, §2.4.1] and twisting); Propositions 6.2.16–6.2.17 (R_v^1 equidimensional of dimension 1 + n² with characteristic-0 generic points and unique generization of generic points of R_v^1/ϖ; R_v^χ irreducible of dimension 1 + n²; "contained in [Tay08, Prop. 3.1]"); Proposition 6.2.21 (R_v^□ a power series ring in n² variables when H²(F_v, ad ρ̄) = 0; proof "left to the reader"); Proposition 6.2.10 ("essentially contained in [Tho15, Prop. 3.14]"); [BLGHT11, Lem. 3.3] (components of completed tensor products).
Proposition 6.2.12 (read, with proof) requires ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial and [F_v:Q_p] > n(n+1)/2 + 1, and uses Lemma 6.2.9 and Lemma 6.2.11 (both read with proofs).
The dimension identity requires g = qn − n²[F⁺:Q] (Proposition 6.2.33 and printed p. 1067); the printed "g = qn − n[F⁺:Q]" on pp. 1070 and 1081 is a misprint (page images PDF pp. 174, 185).
proofSteps: FL (proof of Lemma 6.2.26 as indicated on printed p. 1042): combine the local statements at S_p (formally smooth), R (Props. 6.2.16/6.2.17) and S_a (formally smooth) with [BLGHT11, Lem. 3.3]. nodes.title: What ACC+ proves unconditionally versus what Calegari–Geraghty assumed: derived Ihara avoidance replaces the integral degree-vanishing part of Conjecture B
nodes.statement: Calegari–Geraghty (CG, Invent. Math. 2018) prove their GL_n modularity lifting (Theorem 5.16, Theorem 9.19) assuming Conjecture B for the relevant Taylor–Wiles sets: existence of Hecke-algebra-valued Galois representations r_m; (1) Fontaine–Laffaille at v | p with weights [0,…,n−1]; (2) the Taylor–Wiles local type at v ∈ Q; (3) the inertial characteristic polynomial at v ∈ R; (4)(a) vanishing of H^i(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m)_m unless i ∈ [q₀, q₀ + l₀] and (4)(b) vanishing of the localized boundary cohomology; (5) an isomorphism between level Y and Y₀(Q) cohomology via lim Q_x(V_x)^{k!}. CG use (4) to realize the localized cohomology by perfect complexes D_N concentrated in degrees q₀,…,q₀ + l₀ and then combine their two-system patching Proposition 6.6 with Taylor’s argument to get near-faithfulness of H^{q₀}(Y, K/O)^∨_m over R_S (Theorem 9.19). ACC+ proves unconditional versions of the inputs they need in the CM case — existence of ρ_m modulo a nilpotent ideal (Theorem 2.3.7, from Scholze), the analogue of (1) (Theorem 4.5.1, FL) and of the ordinary condition (Theorem 5.5.1), (3) (Theorem 3.1.1), and the Taylor–Wiles level comparison (Lemma 6.5.9, via [KT17, Lem. 5.4]) — but not (4)(a): ACC+ states that the vanishing conjecture is not resolved. nodes.title: Existence of Taylor–Wiles data of any size q ≥ h¹_{S^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) killing the dual Selmer group, with q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N and v of degree one (ACC+ Lemma 6.2.32)
nodes.statement: Let T ⊆ S. Assume F is CM with maximal totally real subfield F⁺, ζ_p ∉ F, and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is enormous (ACC+ Definition 6.2.29). Let q ≥ h¹_{S^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)), where H¹_{S^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) = ker(H¹(F_S/F, ad ρ̄(1)) → ∏_{v∈S−T} H¹(F_v, ad ρ̄(1))/L_v^⊥). Then for every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum (Q_N, (α_{v,1},…,α_{v,n})_{v∈Q_N}) with (1) #Q_N = q; (2) q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N and v of degree one over Q for each v ∈ Q_N; (3) h¹_{S_{Q_N}^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) = 0.
hypotheses: F CM, ζ_p ∉ F, ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous: no nontrivial p-power order quotient, H⁰ = H¹ = 0 for ad⁰, and a regular semisimple element acting with nonzero invariants on every simple submodule of ad⁰ (enormity implies p ∤ n, which gives ad ρ̄ = k ⊕ ad⁰ ρ̄).
k contains all eigenvalues of elements of ρ̄(G_F) (standing in §6.2.28).

The statement produces exactly q places; the printed proof shows how to kill one Selmer class at a time; adding further places when the group is already zero is not written (the dual Selmer group can only shrink, and infinitely many admissible places exist by the same Chebotarev argument — reviewer remark).
proofSteps: Since D_v = D_v^□ at v ∈ Q_N, L_v = H¹(G_v, ad ρ̄) and H¹_{S_{Q_N}^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) = ker(H¹_{S^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) → ∏_{v∈Q_N} H¹(F_v, ad ρ̄(1))); by induction it suffices, for a cocycle κ representing a nonzero class, to find infinitely many places v of degree one over Q, split in F(ζ_{p^N}), with ρ̄(Frob_v) having n distinct eigenvalues in k and κ|_{G_{F_v}} ≠ 0 (printed p. 1045).

Degree-one places have density one; by Chebotarev density it suffices to find σ ∈ G_{F(ζ_{p^N})} with ρ̄(σ) having distinct k-rational eigenvalues and p_σ κ(σ) ≠ 0, where p_σ: ad ρ̄ → (ad ρ̄)_σ is the σ-equivariant projection (this makes κ|_{G_{F_v}} a non-coboundary) (printed p. 1046).

Case κ ∈ H¹(F_S/F, ad⁰ ρ̄(1)): with H = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) having no p-power quotient, H = ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}); H⁰(H, ad⁰) = 0 and H¹(H, ad⁰) = 0 make restriction to H¹(F_S/L(ζ_{p^N}), ad⁰ ρ̄(1))^{G_F} injective (inflation–restriction twice, L the splitting field of ρ̄); for a nonzero irreducible W in the span of κ(Gal(F_S/L(ζ_{p^N}))) enormity gives σ₀ with distinct k-rational eigenvalues and W^{σ₀} ≠ 0; take σ = σ₀ or σ = τσ₀ with τ ∈ G_{L(ζ_{p^N})} and p_{σ₀}κ(τ) ≠ 0.

Case κ ∈ H¹(F_S/F, k(1)): κ corresponds to a Kummer extension F(ζ_p, y) with y^p ∈ F(ζ_p), non-abelian over F because κ ≠ 0 and ζ_p ∉ F; hence y^p ∉ F(ζ_{p^N}) and κ|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} ≠ 0; the degree-p extension F(ζ_{p^N}, y)/F(ζ_{p^N}) is disjoint from the field cut out by ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_{p^N})}} by enormity, so σ with distinct eigenvalues and κ(σ) ≠ 0 exists.

nodes.statement: Fix a non-principal ultrafilter on N (as in §6.4.1). Put q = h¹(F_S/F, ad ρ̄_m(1)), g = qn − n²[F⁺:Q], Δ_∞ = Z_p^{nq}, Λ = O, T a power series ring over O in n²|S| − 1 variables (framing variables of Lemma 6.2.4), S_∞ = T[[Δ_∞]] with augmentation ideal a_∞; enlarge E to contain ζ_p and choose χ_v pairwise distinct for v ∈ R. For N ≥ 1 choose a Taylor–Wiles datum Q_N by Proposition 6.2.33 (using any imaginary quadratic subfield of F; possible by enormity), Q_0 = ∅, Δ_N = Δ_{Q_N} with a fixed surjection Δ_∞ → Δ_N (kernel in (p^N Z_p)^{nq} because q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N), Δ_0 = 1. Deformation data: R_N = R_{S_{1,Q_N}}, R′_N = R_{S_{χ,Q_N}} (R_0 = R_{S_1}, R′_0 = R_{S_χ}), R^loc = R^{S,loc}_{S_1}, R′^loc = R^{S,loc}_{S_χ} (unchanged by Q_N), canonical isomorphisms R^loc/ϖ ≅ R′^loc/ϖ and R_N/ϖ ≅ R′_N/ϖ, R_N ⊗_{O[Δ_N]} O ≅ R_0, R^loc-algebra structures on R_N ⊗̂_O T (Lemma 6.2.4), R_∞, R′_∞ power series rings in g variables over R^loc, R′^loc, with local surjections R_∞ → R_N, R′_∞ → R′_N compatible with all identifications (Proposition 6.2.25 for N = 0, Proposition 6.2.33(3) for N ≥ 1). Complexes: C_0 = R Hom_O(RΓ(X_K, V_λ(1))_m, O)[−d], T_0 = T^S(K, V_λ(1))_m, C′_0 and T′_0 with V_λ(χ⁻¹); for N ≥ 1, C_N = R Hom_{O[Δ_N]}(RΓ_{K₀(Q_N)/K₁(Q_N)}(X_{K₁(Q_N)}, V_λ(1))_{n^Q_1}, O[Δ_N])[−d] with T_N = _{K₀(Q)/K₁(Q)}T^{S∪Q_N}(…), and C′_N, T′_N with V_λ(χ⁻¹). Verified set-up items: (i) C_N ⊗^L k[Δ_N] ≅ C′_N ⊗^L k[Δ_N] canonically, with T_N, T′_N having the same image T̄_N; (ii) C_N ⊗^L_{O[Δ_N]} O ≅ C_0 and C′_N ⊗^L O ≅ C′_0 compatibly mod ϖ (Lemma 6.5.9); (iii) nilpotent I_N ⊂ T_N, I′_N ⊂ T′_N of exponent ≤ δ with surjections R_N → T_N/I_N, R′_N → T′_N/I′_N compatible mod ϖ (Propositions 6.5.3 and 6.5.11); (iv) T_N ⊗_{O[Δ]} O → T_0 surjective onto T_0/I_0 (Chebotarev density and the Galois representations over T_0/I_0). Output of §6.4.2: bounded complexes C_∞, C′_∞ of free S_∞-modules, T_∞, T′_∞ with I_∞^δ = I′_∞^δ = 0, S_∞-algebra surjections R_∞ → T_∞/I_∞, R′_∞ → T′_∞/I′_∞, surjections R_∞/a_∞ → R_0, R′_∞/a_∞ → R′_0, isomorphisms C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/a_∞ ≅ C_0, C′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/a_∞ ≅ C′_0 inducing T_∞ → T_0 surjective onto T_0/I_0, and C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ ≅ C′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ with common Hecke image and identified R_∞/ϖ ≅ R′_∞/ϖ actions on H*(…)/(Ī_∞ + Ī′_∞).
hypotheses: §6.5.1 hypotheses (1)–(17); in particular enormity of r̄_ι(π)(G_{F(ζ_p)}) and ζ_p ∉ F (H⁰(F_S/F, ad ρ̄_m(1)) = 0 because r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is irreducible and ζ_p ∉ F, used for Proposition 6.2.25 at N = 0).

Boundedness required by ultrapatching (uniform rank and degree bounds for the minimal complexes F(J, N), ACC+ Proposition 6.4.10(1)) is not an extra hypothesis: it follows from C_N ⊗^L Λ ≅ C_0 via rk F(J, N)^i = dim_k H^i(C_0 ⊗^L k) (Definition 6.4.3).

Perfectness of C_N over O[Δ_N]: RΓ_{K₀(Q)/K₁(Q)}(X_{K₁(Q)}, V) is perfect in D(O[K₀(Q)/K₁(Q)]) by ACC+ Lemma 2.1.7 (finite triangulation of the Borel–Serre compactification); localization at n^Q_1 is a direct summand (idempotent decomposition, §1.2).
The ultrafilter is fixed once; independence of the patched complex from the transition-map choices is ACC+ Remark 6.4.13 (P8); no independence from the ultrafilter is claimed.
proofSteps: For each N ≥ 1 choose Q_N by Proposition 6.2.33 and the surjection Δ_∞ → Δ_N; kernel in (p^N Z_p)^{nq} (printed p. 1068).

Deformation side: R_N, R′_N and their identifications modulo ϖ and after ⊗_{O[Δ_N]} O (the latter from a_Q-description in §6.2.28), Lemma 6.2.4 for framings, and the surjections from R_∞ (Proposition 6.2.25 at N = 0 using H⁰(F_S/F, ad ρ̄_m(1)) = 0; Proposition 6.2.33(3) at N ≥ 1, printed as "Proposition 6.2.32"), chosen compatibly with the identifications (printed p. 1068).

nodes.title: Patched automorphy in the Fontaine–Laffaille case: H*(X_K, V_λ(1))_m has full support over R_{S_1}, and lifts of type S_1 are automorphic (ACC+ Theorem 6.5.4 and Corollary 6.5.5)
nodes.statement: Under §6.5.1 (1)–(17): (Theorem 6.5.4) H*(X_K, V_λ(1))_m has full support over R_{S_1}. (Corollary 6.5.5) Let ρ: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) be continuous with ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π); ρ|_{G_{F_v}} crystalline with HT_τ(ρ) = {λ_{ιτ,1} + n − 1, …, λ_{ιτ,n}} for each v | p and τ: F ↪ Q̄_p; ρ|_{G_{F_v}} unramified for v ∉ S; ρ|_{G_{F_v}} unipotently ramified for v ∈ R. Then there is a cuspidal regular algebraic automorphic representation Π of weight λ with ρ ≅ r_ι(Π), and Π_v is unramified if v | p or v ∉ S.
hypotheses: All of §6.5.1 (1)–(17). The full-support conclusion is a statement about supports (reduced structure), not an integral R = T theorem.

The ultrafilter patching (P8), Taylor–Wiles data (this stage), the support implication (PA.3) and Theorem 2.4.10 (PA.0) are the ingredients; local–global compatibility inputs (Theorems 3.1.1, 4.5.1) enter through Propositions 6.5.3 and 6.5.11.
The soluble base change reduction (§6.5.12, Proposition 6.5.13 from [AC89]) and the deduction of Theorem 6.1.1 are outside this node (final assembly owned by ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions).
proofSteps: Theorem 6.5.4: build the patching set-up for (S_1, S_χ) with χ_v pairwise distinct (arithmetic set-up node), apply ACC+ §6.4.2 to get (C_∞, C′_∞, T_∞, T′_∞, R_∞, R′_∞) with C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/a_∞ ≅ C_0, then apply the FL generic support implication (PA.3): Assumption 6.3.6 holds and H*(C_0), hence H*(X_K, V_λ(1))_m, has full support over R_{S_1} (printed pp. 1067–1070).

Corollary 6.5.5: enlarge E and conjugate so ρ is valued in GL_n(O) with ρ mod ϖ = ρ̄_m; ρ is a lift of type S_1 (crystalline with the given Hodge–Tate weights gives type D_v^FL, unipotent ramification gives D_v^1), giving f: R_{S_1} → E (printed p. 1064).

By Theorem 6.5.4, ker f lies in the support of H*(X_K, V_λ(1))_m[1/p]; Theorem 2.4.10 then gives Π cuspidal regular algebraic of weight λ with ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) and (Π^∞)^K ≠ 0, hence Π_v unramified where K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}), i.e. v | p or v ∉ S (printed p. 1064).
acceptance: Keep hypotheses and conclusions exactly: crystalline with the stated Hodge–Tate multiset (Fontaine–Laffaille range guaranteed by (8) and p > n²), unipotent ramification on R, unramified outside S.
The final automorphy lifting Theorem 6.1.1 requires the additional soluble base change of §6.5.12; do not attribute it to this node.
